$comment: Answer-coverage ledger for factory/ci/Test-SchemaCoverage.ps1. Two lists, and the difference between them matters. consumedIndirectly names answers that DO reach a delivered artifact through a consumer that reads them structurally rather than by dotted name — the coverage scan cannot see them, but the client gets what they answered. recordedNotDeployed names answers that reach nothing but lz-config.json: the client is asked, the answer is preserved, and no estate is built from it. That second list is debt, it carries a budget that only ratchets down, and every entry owes a reason and a way out. It is now EMPTY: every answer the wizard collects reaches a delivered artifact. Six groups closed on 2026-08-31 by rendering them into the generated repository's documentation rather than by deploying anything — a spoke address range or an ExpressRoute circuit order is a decision the estate team acts on, not a resource this factory creates, and writing it down is the whole of the fix. A new entry here is a regression, not a routine addition.

consumedIndirectly.note: Reads the plannedNames map whole ($subs['plannedNames']) and iterates its slots, so no slot is ever named in source. The wizard derives these from organization.companyShortName; they become the display names of the subscriptions the vending run creates.
Read through Get-LzConfigValue against the branchProtection object rather than by path, and applied to the generated repository as required_linear_history.

Resolve-LzPolicySelection walks the policySelection object by key to build policy_assignment_changes, so the group ids and assignment names — which come from the generated ALZ catalog, not from the schema — are never spelled in source.

The wizard blocks export when it is false, because it can only be true: the broker creates the state account with --allow-shared-key-access false, and every emitted backend.hcl and remote-state block sets use_azuread_auth = true unconditionally. Read as b.azurerm.useAzureAdAuth in validate(), which is why the dotted path appears nowhere. It stays in the schema so an imported configuration that says otherwise is caught rather than silently corrected; retiring it is a schema major.

Resolve-LzManagementGroups reads it off the managementGroups object by key to choose which landing-zone group the workload subscriptions are placed under, so the dotted path appears nowhere. It selects corp, online, or landingzones directly; the chosen group is then renamed along with the rest of the hierarchy and emitted as workload_management_group_id.

Read off the hcpTerraform object by key in validate(), which is why the dotted path appears nowhere. It gates export: with the HCP Terraform backend selected and the estimated resource count above the free tier's 500, the wizard refuses to export until it is ticked. Like backend.azurerm.useAzureAdAuth it reaches no rendered artifact by design — its purpose is to be the record that the client was shown the cap, sitting beside the estimate in deployment-metadata.json.

Walked structurally into computed.nonProdSpokes and rendered as a table by docs/CONNECTIVITY.md.tmpl. The environment keys are iterated as a list (dev/test/uat) rather than named individually, so no dotted path appears in source. The client gets what they answered: per ADR 0017 no layer builds a workload spoke, so the deliverable for an addressing decision is the decision, written down where the estate team building the spoke will read it.

Flattened into computed.finopsBudgets and rendered as a table by docs/FINOPS.md.tmpl, which previously named finops.budgets in prose and rendered no field of it. Each budget is an array element, so the fields are reached off the object rather than by dotted name. The document states plainly that no Microsoft.Consumption budget is created by any layer — the table is the requirement, not the state.

Flattened into computed.approvalChain and rendered as a table by docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md.tmpl. Array elements, so the fields are reached off the object. The generated workflows' environment protection rules are the mechanism; this table is who is expected to act on them, and the two are kept in step by hand.

Read off the resolved defaultSubscriptionBudget object by Resolve-LzDefaultBudget and written into lib/policy_assignments/Deploy-Budget.alz_policy_assignment.json as that policy's own parameter names — amountUsd becomes amount, timeGrain becomes timeGrain, contactEmails and contactRoles keep theirs. No dotted path appears in source because the object is resolved once and its fields read off it, the same shape as finops.budgets above. Unlike finops.budgets, these DO reach a deployed resource: Deploy-Budget is a DeployIfNotExists that creates the Microsoft.Consumption budget on every subscription under the assigned management group. Asserted field by field in Test-Renderer section 12g, including that amount and both thresholds are emitted as JSON strings, which is what the policy declares them as.
